html:
The invasion of Poland began on 1 September 1939, when Germany attacked Poland from the north, west and south. The Soviet Union invaded from the east on 17 September. Poland was overrun in five weeks, and World War II in Europe had begun.

Hitler wanted the city of Danzig and the land that cut East Prussia off from the rest of Germany, and beyond that room to settle Germans in the east. In August 1939 he and Stalin signed the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact, which secretly divided Poland between them. Britain and France had promised to defend Poland and declared war on 3 September, but did not attack Germany in force. About 1.5 million German troops, with some 2,700 tanks and 2,300 aircraft, broke through the Polish lines and closed around the Polish armies. The Poles hit back on the Bzura River but were surrounded. Warsaw surrendered on 28 September, and the last large Polish unit on 6 October.

About 66,000 Polish soldiers were killed. Germany and the Soviet Union split the country. Poland never formally surrendered: its government and many soldiers fought on from abroad. The occupation that followed killed nearly six million Polish citizens, about half of them Jews.
sum: The invasion of Poland began on 1 September 1939, when Germany attacked Poland from the north, west and south. The Soviet Union invaded from the east on 17 September. Poland was overrun in five weeks, and World War II in Europe had begun.
